review.summary:
Attempt 5 of the phase-governance chunk closes all six attempt-04 findings and every governance-scoped finding from the rejected phase attempt-02, each by strengthening the gate rather than softening a claim, and the recorded check evidence is genuine, complete and source-bound.

Fix verification (all against current source, not prose): (1) deny.toml is now in the phase-21 frozen-input list at tools/check_phase.py:148 — it appears in the recorded baseline diff (docs/checks/phase-21.json:20) and in the untracked-file assertion built from the same `paths` list (check_phase.py:158-160), with tools/test_management_phases.py:23 asserting it; docs/PHASES.md:221-222 additionally states deny.toml must remain byte-identical so a passing audit cannot authorize a relaxed policy. (2) tools/test_management_phases.py:174-178 replaced the list-membership checks with argument-level substring checks (`any("0.2.2" in value for command in commands for value in command)` plus per-value `assertNotIn("docs/checks/phase-19-"/"phase-20-")`), closing the precision gap for the inherited phase-22-25 command lists. (3) tools/test_ci.py:496-501 now resolves the contracts job step list and asserts `lines.index("run: python3 tools/bootstrap_reference.py") < lines.index(gate)` whenever any selected command's argv[0] resolves under .local/typescript/node_modules or tools/node_modules — exactly the required fix, and satisfied by .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:70-73. (4) the hand-maintained manifest-consumer list is replaced by derived discovery in test_every_manifest_reader_is_selected_or_explicitly_explained (test_management_phases.py:150-165), which computes literal `contracts/manifest.json` readers under tools/ and requires each to be selected by commands_for(21) or carry a nonempty, reviewed exemption string; g25_audit.py's frozen-baseline-commit justification is now recorded in the repository. (5) docs/PHASES.md:135 now names the current dependency/advisory audit and the baseline-to-HEAD committed hygiene check, and :219-222 records the resulting network and full-history prerequisites, so the authoritative phase table is no longer the least current of the three scoped documents. (6) the glued-digit typography is normalised across docs/PHASES.md, docs/CI.md and docs/RELEASE.md (verified by targeted regex sweeps returning only legitimate version/commit strings), while the guarded count sentences remain in their asserted form at test_ci.py:119-128 and :135-146. The phase-attempt-02 low asking to derive fetch-depth purely from range presence is also fixed: the `phase == 21 or` disjunct is gone from test_ci.py:49-53.

Evidence is real and consistent. docs/reviews/phase-21-chunk-phase-governance-attempt-05.checks.json is content-identical to docs/checks/phase-21.json (same checked_at 13:51:33.914794, same 25 entries head to tail), carries source_sha256 bc704b5f… equal to my reviewed fingerprint, source_unchanged true, passed true and no `scope` key, so review_phase.check_evidence:210-217 would accept it and would reject a contracts-only receipt. I reconstructed commands_for(21) by hand from check_phase.py:135-175 (4 phase-specific commands, the 10-command `common` block in order, then check-dependencies, test_ci, the three `--check` tools, verify_native_fixtures, red_team_dataplane, the two tsx oracles, generate_validation, generate_models) and it matches the 25 recorded entries element for element and in order; every exit_code is 0 with timeout false. Captured stderr shows test_red_team_management 32/32, test_management_phases 22/22, test_review_phase 51/51 and test_ci 35/35 green — the counts match the suites as they exist on disk. The dependency audit is a real execution, not a stub: docs/checks/phase-21-dependencies.json records cargo-audit 0.22.2 and cargo-deny 0.20.2 binary digests, a fetched RustSec revision 999ec89d… with freshHead true, 1338 advisories, 206 resolved packages, zero vulnerabilities and a clean bans/licenses/sources summary, with policySha256 pinned. The private-material scan ran 29 seconds before the gate at the identical fingerprint (1907 git-visible files, zero identity/secret matches, zero new tenant occurrences). docs/phase-status.json:5097-5134 records this chunk's three immutable scope revisions (from_attempt 1/3/4; 4, 8 and 9 paths) and my prompt's nine artifacts match the from_attempt-4 revision exactly in order; the per-review `decisions` map records attempt-02 as rejected at 41/50, and private_scan_history now gives each of the eight superseded receipts its own specific cause.

The governance design itself holds up. declared_chunk_scope:228-249 requires ordered unique revisions starting at from_attempt 1 whose last entry equals the current scope and resolves a historical attempt to the revision then in force; verify_attempt_sequence:125-130 re-checks each prior record against that revision and against the exact `Chunk scope artifacts: [...]` line in its preserved prompt, so inserting, rewriting or narrowing any revision invalidates rather than silently rebinds an accepted record. gate_decision:69-86 defaults completed_prior to 0, rejects on any blocker/high before scoring, targets 42 for chunks and 46 for phases, grants accepted_with_deficiencies only at attempt 5 with exactly four completed priors, every category >=8 and a recorded finding or limitation, and line 70 independently rejects any phase-21 phase-level review below 9/10; verify_record:272-275 recomputes the decision with the real count so a fabricated decision cannot carry gate_passed true. Failed invocations `continue` without incrementing completed (89-106), and every prior-attempt artifact read is guarded by `not is_file() or is_symlink()`. Later phases stay fail-closed: red_team_management.py:602-603 raises unconditionally for --require-through-phase above 21, management_commands drops the 0.2.2-specific release helper (check_phase.py:186) and rewrites inherited phase-19/20 receipt paths, and phase 21 deliberately omits native_exports/live_evidence per the documented evidence-scope boundary at docs/PHASES.md:195-203. The CI subset cannot qualify a review even though it currently equals the full 25 commands, because check_phase.main:691-694 stamps the contracts scope marker and writes a separate receipt.

What remains is small and all low: the reviewer prompt template itself still carries the glued-digit defect the proofreading fix removed from the three scoped documents ("strictly above40", "remains46/50", "Phase20") and reaches the reviewer verbatim; the phase-21 note at docs/phase-status.json:5160 was named in the required fix but not normalised; the baseline-to-HEAD ranged check is vacuous in this source state because HEAD still equals MANAGEMENT_BASELINE, so its recorded exit 0 proves nothing yet and the real coverage comes from the uncommitted and staged diffs; a failed Claude invocation on attempt 5 would consume the last budgeted attempt and leave the chunk unadvanceable with no documented remedy; and the derived manifest-reader discovery is non-recursive and does not scan scripts/. No blocker, high or medium finding. Categories 9/9/8.5/9/9 = 44.5/50, which clears the chunk target of 42 with every category >=8 without needing the fifth-attempt exception.

findings.description: The proofreading fix requested by attempt-04 finding 6 and phase attempt-02 was applied to docs/PHASES.md, docs/CI.md and docs/RELEASE.md but not to the prompt template in this same scoped file, which is the text actually sent to the reviewer. Line 521 emits "a total strictly above40 may proceed" and line 539 "The phase threshold remains46/50"; lines 406, 418 and 542 emit "Phase20"/"phase20" in argparse help and error text, and tools/check_phase.py:185 carries "the phase24 milestone gate" in a comment. My own prompt (docs/reviews/phase-21-chunk-phase-governance-attempt-05.prompt.md:33) contains the defect verbatim, so the rubric sentence a reviewer reads under time pressure is the least legible copy of it. Nothing is functionally wrong and no guarded count regex matches these sentences, but the fix is incomplete inside the chunk's own scope.
findings.required_fix: Normalise the spacing before numerals in the prompt and diagnostic strings at tools/review_phase.py:406, 418, 521, 539, 542 and the comment at tools/check_phase.py:185, keeping the guarded count sentences in docs/CI.md unchanged so test_ci.py:119-128 and :135-146 continue to match.

findings.description: The attempt-04 required fix explicitly named "the phase-21 notes in docs/phase-status.json" as part of the spacing normalisation. That note still reads "All phase attempt01 and chunk03 findings resolved. Current chunk attempt04 accepted: provenance45/50 score9, governance44.5/50 score9". Unlike the historical phase-20 record at :4997 ("and49-job CI completed"), which is immutable accepted evidence, this is live phase-21 bookkeeping that the next phase review is instructed to read. phase-status.json is excluded from the source fingerprint (review_phase.py:16) and is not in this chunk's declared scope, so I record it as a residual deficiency of the cross-cutting fix rather than a defect in a scoped artifact.
findings.required_fix: Rewrite the phase-21 review_findings_disposition note with normal spacing before numerals ("attempt 01", "chunk 03", "provenance 45/50 score 9", "governance 44.5/50 score 9"), leaving historical phase records untouched.

findings.description: The committed-range hygiene check `git diff --check 0a213fe79c7f0c5758f05f53d04a5c577a4f3f4e..HEAD -- . :(exclude)…yaml` is currently a no-op: docs/checks/phase-21-private-material.json:5 records headCommit 0a213fe79c7f0c5758f05f53d04a5c577a4f3f4e, i.e. HEAD still equals MANAGEMENT_BASELINE, so the range is empty and the recorded exit 0 for check 4 (docs/checks/phase-21.json:89-117) demonstrates nothing about the phase-21 changes. All actual coverage in this source state comes from the unranged `git diff --check` and `git diff --cached --check` commands over the worktree and index. The design is sound — the fingerprint is commit-independent, so the check becomes meaningful once the staged work is committed without invalidating this review — but docs/PHASES.md:219-220 and docs/CI.md:146-148 present the ranged check as current evidence and require full Git history for it, which is not yet what the receipt shows.
findings.required_fix: Note in docs/CI.md's Phase 21 paragraph (around :145-148) that the ranged check is vacuous until the planning work is committed and that worktree/index hygiene is carried by the two unranged diffs, or add an assertion that the recorded range is non-empty when the phase gate is run for review, so a passing receipt is not read as committed-range proof.

findings.description: A failed Claude invocation on attempt 5 is an undocumented dead end for a chunk. failed_invocation (556-562) writes a sanitized receipt and consumes the attempt; main:422-423 then raises "The review loop allows at most five attempts" for any attempt 6; verify_attempt_sequence:95-106 correctly refuses to count the failure as a completed review, so the fifth-attempt >40 exception cannot be reached either; and accepted_chunks:348-370 requires an accepted latest record and restricts the phase-followup path to `record.get("attempt") == 5` with an accepted record (357-360). docs/PHASES.md:157-167 states only that "the five-attempt ceiling still applies" and :216-217 that failure to supply substantive-review history never enables the exception. The net effect is a chunk that can never advance, with no recorded maintainer remedy.
findings.required_fix: Document the remedy in docs/PHASES.md's review-invocation-failure section — e.g. that a maintainer may authorize a new chunk id or a new scope revision with a fresh budget, with the prior attempts retained as history — and add a test asserting the chosen remedy, so an attempt-5 invocation failure has a defined path instead of an undocumented dead end.

findings.description: test_every_manifest_reader_is_selected_or_explicitly_explained correctly replaces the hand-maintained list with derived discovery, but the derivation is narrower than the guarantee it implies: it iterates `(ROOT / "tools").iterdir()` non-recursively and does not look at scripts/. I confirmed the result is correct today — ripgrep finds no `contracts/manifest.json` reader under scripts/, and tools/ has no owned subpackage (only node_modules and __pycache__, both excluded by the suffix filter). The gap is that a future manifest-consuming checker added under scripts/ or a tools subdirectory would escape the derived coverage while the test still passes, which is the exact failure mode the derivation was introduced to prevent.
findings.required_fix: Widen the discovery to `ROOT.rglob` over the owned tool and script trees (tools/ and scripts/, excluding node_modules, __pycache__ and test_* files) so any new literal contracts/manifest.json consumer must be selected by commands_for(21) or added to the commented exemption map.

evidence: Recorded check evidence is complete, executed and source-bound. docs/reviews/phase-21-chunk-phase-governance-attempt-05.checks.json is content-identical to docs/checks/phase-21.json (identical header through checked_at 2026-10-19T13:51:33.914794 and identical final entry at :528-544), reports phase 21, source_sha256 bc704b5f8a8dae6f358a32391765e462af5ca9c0d7dab44f4c7b24436e450b24 equal to the reviewed fingerprint in my prompt, source_unchanged true, passed true, and carries no "scope" key, so review_phase.check_evidence:210-217 accepts it and would reject the contracts-only receipt. I reconstructed commands_for(21) by hand from tools/check_phase.py:135-175 and it matches the 25 recorded entries element for element and in order; every exit_code is 0 and every timeout false.

Attempt-04 finding 1 (deny.toml) is fixed structurally. tools/check_phase.py:148 includes "deny.toml" in the phase-21 `paths` list, which feeds both the baseline diff (155-156) and the untracked-file assertion (158-160); the recorded diff command at docs/checks/phase-21.json:20 and the ls-files command at :76 both contain it; tools/test_management_phases.py:23 asserts `assertIn("deny.toml", commands[0])`; and docs/PHASES.md:221-222 states deny.toml remains byte-identical to the audited baseline alongside Cargo inputs so a passing audit cannot silently authorize a relaxed dependency policy.

Attempt-04 findings 2 and 3 are fixed exactly as required. tools/test_management_phases.py:174 now reads `self.assertFalse(any("0.2.2" in value for command in commands for value in command))` and :175-178 iterate per-argument `assertNotIn("docs/checks/phase-19-"/"phase-20-", value)`, so a rewritten-but-still-version-bound argument cannot pass. tools/test_ci.py:496-501 resolves the contracts job's step lines and asserts `lines.index("run: python3 tools/bootstrap_reference.py") < lines.index(gate)` conditioned on any selected command's argv[0] starting with .local/typescript/node_modules/ or tools/node_modules/ — both phase-21 tsx oracles qualify, and .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:70-73 places the restore step before the gate.

Attempt-04 finding 4 is fixed by derivation, not by a longer list. tools/test_management_phases.py:150-165 computes the set of tools/ files whose text contains the literal contracts/manifest.json, requires each to be either an argument of commands_for(21) or present in a four-entry exemption map, asserts the exemptions are a subset of the discovered readers and that every exemption carries a nonempty reason, and records g25_audit.py's justification ("Reads only the frozen baseline commit, validated by verify-contracts") in the repository for the first time.

Attempt-04 findings 5 and 6 are fixed in the documents. docs/PHASES.md:135 now names "current dependency/advisory audit, baseline-to-HEAD committed hygiene check" alongside the pre-existing evidence, and :219-222 records the resulting network (RustSec refresh) and full-history prerequisites plus the deny.toml freeze. Targeted regex sweeps for glued numerals across docs/PHASES.md, docs/CI.md and docs/RELEASE.md return only legitimate version and commit strings (v4.3.1, v6.6.0, release-tag-v0.2.2.json), and the previously cited sites now read "at least 46/50", "phase 18 accepts", "phases 21–25", "management 0.86.0 bytes", "the frozen 0.2.2 baseline" and "its 59-command full gate and 41-command contracts subset".

The phase attempt-02 CI low is also closed. tools/test_ci.py:49-53 derives the fetch-depth requirement purely from whether any selected command is a `git diff --check` carrying a `..` range, with no `phase == 21` disjunct, and asserts `fetch-depth:\s*0` in the checkout block (satisfied by .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:25); test_current_dependency_audit_and_committed_hygiene_are_required (test_management_phases.py:338-341) remains the separate assertion that phase 21 actually has such a range. test_committed_range_fails_on_shallow_history_and_passes_after_full_fetch (test_ci.py:69-90) is a real git-subprocess regression over a depth-1 clone, not a string check.

The dependency audit is a genuine execution with a frozen policy. docs/checks/phase-21-dependencies.json records cargo-audit 0.22.2 and cargo-deny 0.20.2 with binary SHA-256 digests, an actual fetch of RustSec advisory-db to revision 999ec89d5d3f10f20be14750ec8c2d8b44e0ac9b with upstreamHeadAtFetch equal and freshHead true, lockfileUnchanged true with lockfileSha256 785e16a5…, policySha256 b4636311…, 1338 advisories against 206 resolved packages with vulnerabilities.found false and empty warnings, and a cargo-deny summary of zero errors/warnings for bans, licenses and sources. docs/CI.md:152-156 lists exactly check-dependencies.py and check-private-material.py, and tools/test_ci.py:60-67 asserts that documented inventory equals the executed subset's scripts/check-*.py set with both present and no phase-21 exemption, so .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:62-69 has a real consumer.

Scope governance is versioned and immutable per attempt. review_phase.declared_chunk_scope:228-249 requires a nonempty ordered scope_revisions list starting at from_attempt 1 with unique nonempty paths whose last revision equals the current scope, and resolves a historical attempt to the revision in force then; verify_attempt_sequence:125-130 re-checks each prior record against that revision and against the exact `Chunk scope artifacts: [...]` line in its preserved prompt; verify_record:292-298 does the same for the record under test. docs/phase-status.json:5097-5134 records this chunk's revisions (from_attempt 1/3/4 with 4, 8 and 9 paths), and the nine artifacts in my prompt match the from_attempt-4 revision exactly and in order. test_scope_revision_history_preserves_old_reviews_and_rejects_rewrites proves that rewriting revision 1 invalidates the attempt-01 record and that dropping a revision raises. All ten chunks declared for phases 21-25 carry scope_revisions.

The fifth-attempt exception and the plan-score floor are strict and independently enforced. gate_decision:69-86 defaults completed_prior to 0, rejects on any blocker/high finding before scoring, targets 42 for chunks and 46 for phases, grants accepted_with_deficiencies only when attempt == 5 and completed_prior == 4 and total > 40 and every category >= 8 and a finding or limitation exists, and line 70 rejects any phase-21 phase-level review scoring below 9/10. verify_record:272-275 recomputes the decision with the real prior count and rejects a mismatch, and line 278 additionally requires gate_passed true, so a rejected review cannot be relabelled. test_failed_attempts_cannot_unlock_fifth_exception asserts rejection at total 41 for 0-3 completed priors and acceptance only at 4; test_plan_score_floor_cannot_be_bypassed_by_category_total asserts a 50/50 review scoring 8.5/10 fails verify_record for phase 21.

Later phases cannot pass on plan artifacts, and the inherited lists are sanitized. tools/red_team_management.py:599-603 restricts --require-through-phase to 21-25 and raises unconditionally above 21; management_commands adds that flag for 22-25, skips scripts/check-access-release.py when inheriting (check_phase.py:186), rewrites inherited phase-19/20 receipt paths to the active phase (188-189), re-adds the vendor whitespace exclusion to inherited ranged diffs (190-194) and appends both packaged compilers from phase 23 (197-200). test_future_milestones_require_explicit_complete_artifacts, test_qualification_has_both_packaged_compilers, test_vendor_whitespace_is_excluded_from_all_new_hygiene_checks and test_plan_retains_static_closure_without_claiming_current_live_proof cover these across phases 21-25.

The single SDK-file exception is byte-exact and its CI subset cannot qualify a review. require_only_hash_replacements:79-90 requires each replaced value to be 64 lowercase hex characters occurring exactly once and then compares full reconstructed bytes; verify_planning_fixture:93-120 applies it to crates/scm-sdk/src/fixtures/model-regressions.json, resolves the corpus path from the baseline object so "source" cannot be redirected, rejects symlinks and requires the rebound manifest hash to equal current contracts/manifest.json bytes; verify_planning_gateway_proof:123-132 allows exactly the two allowlisted input hashes and fails closed if the allowlist is incomplete (test_gateway_proof_allows_only_two_rebound_input_hashes drives reordering and a third rebound hash). check_phase.main:691-694 stamps scope "ci_contracts_only_not_full_phase_qualification" on the separate phase-21-contracts.json, and test_ci_subsets_cannot_replace_full_reports asserts that receipt is rejected as "incomplete" for all five phases.

Privacy evidence is fresh at the reviewed hash and the documents are mutually consistent. docs/checks/phase-21-private-material.json records checkedAt 13:51:04 (29 seconds before the gate's 13:51:33), sourceSha256 bc704b5f… identical to the reviewed fingerprint, sourceUnchanged true, passed true, 1907 git-visible files, zero identity/secret matches, 132 published-crate candidates with zero registration matches and three tenant occurrences all pre-existing in HEAD with newOrChangedFilesCount 0, with its --check limitation (no re-execution of private matching) stated explicitly. On job counts, ci.yml's 2 toolchains x 24 feature sets + 1 = 49 matches docs/CI.md:4 ("Its 49 required jobs"), :111 ("each run 24 feature selections (48 jobs total)"), :163-164 ("48-job Rust matrix … 49 required jobs") and docs/RELEASE.md:9 and :30, all guarded by test_current_documented_job_counts_match_the_configured_matrix and test_current_documented_gate_command_counts_match_selected_commands.
limitations: Read-only review with no execution. I could not compute any SHA-256, run git, or run the suites, so the reviewed source hash bc704b5f…, the stated checks snapshot hash ebd06b6f…, the private-material and dependency receipt bindings and all 25 recorded exit codes are judged from the preserved prompt, the recorded snapshots and the source of the tools that produced them. My statement that the recorded command list equals commands_for(21) is a hand reconstruction of tools/check_phase.py:135-175, and my statement that the attempt-05 checks snapshot equals docs/checks/phase-21.json is a content comparison of its header, entry sequence and tail, not a byte or digest comparison.

No remote run of the re-pointed workflow exists. docs/checks/ contains no phase-21-contracts.json, so the phase-21 CI routing is committed configuration plus local guard evidence only, and the job now additionally depends on network access for the RustSec advisory refresh and on a restored .local/typescript tree for the two tsx oracles. docs/CI.md:164-165 and :218-219 and docs/PHASES.md:174-180 state this honestly and phase 21's acceptance criteria do not require remote CI, so I treat it as unverified configuration rather than a finding.

The review evidence chain is self-referential by design. review_phase.py:15-16 excludes docs/reviews/, docs/checks/ and docs/phase-status.json from the source fingerprint, so record, prompt, CLI-envelope, snapshot and chunk-declaration integrity rests on hashes recorded inside those same unfingerprinted files; a consistently edited set is undetectable from inside this review. docs/PHASES.md:7 states explicitly that repository writers and the reviewer tool are trusted and that these hashes detect staleness rather than authenticating the CLI process. The scope_revisions mechanism closes the retroactive-rewrite path within that model; the model itself is pre-existing and unchanged.

Scope was the nine declared phase-governance artifacts. I did not audit the plan-and-provenance chunk (contracts/airs-*.json, the vendored 0.86.0 tree, manifest ownership, tools/red_team_management.py internals beyond its --require-through-phase fail-closed path and the manifest-consumer question), and its sibling attempt-05 prompt and checks snapshot exist without a completed or failed receipt, so I make no claim about it. I verified only the governance claims that depend on it.

I did not re-audit historical phase command lists beyond the inherited ones phases 22-25 reuse. I read commands_for(17)/(19)/(20) enough to confirm that no phase-12, phase-17, phase-19 or phase-20 receipt path and no 0.2.2 literal can leak into a management phase, but I could not execute the inherited phase-22-25 lists, which fail closed by design.

Static governance evidence only. Nothing in this chunk certifies runtime behaviour, request construction, generated Rust correctness, union-order preservation, dependency advisory status at any later moment, live tenant acceptance, release readiness or phase 22-25 progress. My finding that the baseline-to-HEAD ranged check is currently vacuous rests on docs/checks/phase-21-private-material.json:5 recording headCommit equal to MANAGEMENT_BASELINE; I could not run git to confirm the branch head directly.
